title: Virtual Cards for Business: How They Work, Types and What to Look For
summary: How virtual cards for business work, the main types, the controls to set and a checklist to choose a provider. Includes Jeeves pre-funded virtual cards.
body_markdown:
If your team pays for subscriptions, ads and vendors with one or two shared cards, or waits on slow reimbursements, it is hard to see who spent what and why. Virtual cards for business solve part of that: each one is a digital card number with its own limit, so spending stays tied to a person, a vendor or a project. This guide explains how virtual corporate cards work, the main types, the controls worth asking for and how to choose a provider, using Jeeves pre-funded virtual cards as one example.


## Key takeaways


- A virtual card for business is a digital card number with its own limit that finance assigns to a person, vendor or subscription.
- Virtual corporate cards work best when each card has one purpose, a limit and an end date.
- A pre-funded virtual card spends only money that is already loaded, which is different from cards that draw on a line repaid later.
- Controls per card (limits, merchant category, vendor and dates) matter more than the number of cards.
- Jeeves issues pre-funded virtual cards in the US, drawn from your Jeeves Cash balance.


## What are virtual cards for business?


A virtual card for business is a digital card number issued for company spending, with no physical plastic. Finance teams assign it to an employee, contractor, vendor, project or subscription, set a limit and can close it without affecting any other card.


Because each card has its own number, the transactions on it are easy to trace. If one card is used for a single software subscription, every charge on that card belongs to that subscription.


People who typically use corporate virtual cards include finance teams that want to separate spending by purpose, marketing teams that pay for ad accounts, and operations teams that pay online vendors. Virtual cards for business can sit next to physical cards, so teams that also need a card in hand can mix both formats under the same controls.


## How do virtual corporate cards work?


Virtual corporate cards work in a few steps: a finance admin creates a card in a dashboard, names it, sets a limit and dates, shares the card details or adds the card to a mobile wallet, and every payment is tied to that card.


A typical flow looks like this:


1. Create the card and give it a clear name, such as the vendor or project.
2. Set the limit and, if needed, the start and end dates.
3. Share the details with the person who pays, or add the card to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet.
4. Review each transaction against the card's purpose.
5. Match the receipt and reconcile at close.


Jeeves lets finance teams issue virtual cards for a subscription, an ad account or a one-off purchase, and employees can add them to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet. Finance can see spending and change limits in real time from the same place, as described on the[Jeeves corporate cards](https://www.tryjeeves.com/us-product/corporate-cards) page.


## What types of virtual cards for business are there?


The most common types of virtual cards for business are single-use, recurring-subscription, employee and vendor or project cards. The difference is in how long the card lives and what it is meant to pay for.


Type What it is for Typical setup


Single-use One purchase, such as a one-off vendor payment Limit set to the expected amount, closed after use


Recurring subscription A software or media subscription that renews Fixed limit, one merchant, no end date or a review date


Employee Day-to-day spending by a team member Monthly limit and allowed merchant categories


Vendor or project A supplier or a time-bound project Limit and end date matched to the contract or project


These are generic types, and a provider may group them differently. With Jeeves, you can name each virtual card so it becomes its own cost center, which makes it easy to apply any of these types. If you issue many corporate virtual cards, naming them consistently saves time at close.


## Virtual credit cards vs pre-funded virtual cards: what is the difference?


A virtual credit card draws on a credit line that is repaid later, while a pre-funded virtual card spends only money that has already been loaded. The difference matters because it changes where the money comes from, who is responsible for repayment and whether a credit review is needed.


In general, virtual cards come in several funding models:


- **Pre-funded (prepaid):** you load funds first, and the card can spend only that balance.
- **Debit:** the card draws directly from a business account balance.
- **Charge:** the card is repaid in full on a set schedule.
- **Credit:** the card draws on a credit line, and the amount is repaid later, often with a credit review upfront.


In the US, Jeeves virtual cards are pre-funded: they draw from your Jeeves Cash balance, which you load in USD, CAD, GBP or EUR, and there is no credit line behind them. For a deeper comparison of card types, see[business vs corporate credit cards explained](https://www.tryjeeves.com/blog/corporate-vs-business-credit-card) .


## What controls should virtual corporate cards have?


Virtual corporate cards should let finance set limits per card and control where and when each card can be used. Controls matter more than the number of cards, because they are what turns a card number into a spending policy.


A useful checklist:


- Limits per card, employee, merchant category, vendor or period.
- Hard caps that block spending and soft caps that flag it.
- Start and end dates for each card.
- Allow-lists and block-lists for merchants.
- The ability to freeze or delete a card at any time.


Jeeves lets teams set limits per employee, per merchant category, per vendor or per period, with allow-lists and block-lists, hard or soft caps and start and end dates. Limit changes apply in real time. If your team is still deciding who can approve what, define the policy first and then reflect it in the card settings, starting with a few cards and expanding once the rules work. For more ideas, see these[expense management tips for better control](https://www.tryjeeves.com/blog/expense-management-tips-for-better-control-in-your-company) .


## Are virtual cards safe for business spending?


Virtual cards are generally safer than sharing one card across a team, because each card has its own number, limit and controls. If a card is exposed or no longer needed, finance can freeze or delete it without disrupting other payments.


Safety also comes from isolating spend. A card meant for one vendor can be limited to that vendor's category and amount, so a mistake or misuse stays small.


Good habits help as much as the technology: give each card one purpose, set an end date when the need is temporary, review the transaction list regularly and close cards that are no longer used.


No card removes risk entirely, so pair virtual cards with a clear spending policy and with receipt collection. Your finance lead can also decide who is allowed to see full card details and who only needs to see the transactions.


## What payments are virtual cards best for?


Virtual cards are best for online and recurring payments that need clear ownership: software subscriptions, advertising accounts, cloud services, one-off purchases and online vendors. They also work for travel when a card is added to a mobile wallet.


Each of these payments benefits from the same idea: one card, one purpose, one limit. A subscription card can be capped at the plan price, an ad-account card at the campaign budget and a travel card at the trip budget.


Jeeves cards are optimized for platforms such as Google Ads, AWS, Stripe and Shopify, and for international platforms that routinely decline cards issued outside their home market. Acceptance still depends on each platform's own rules.


For teams that also pay suppliers abroad, the guide on[paying international vendors and suppliers](https://www.tryjeeves.com/blog/paying-international-vendors-suppliers) covers other payment methods. For corporate travel, the right card type depends on the trip, so decide the limit and dates before each trip.


## How do virtual cards work for teams in several countries?


Virtual cards work for teams in several countries when one provider can issue local cards and show them in one dashboard. Jeeves issues local cards in the US, Canada, the UK, Europe, Mexico, Brazil and Colombia, managed from a single dashboard.


A single dashboard helps finance see every card, limit and transaction without switching tools. A regional manager can hold cards in the local market, while finance keeps the same controls and naming across countries.


Card issuance, currencies and features depend on availability in each market and your plan, so confirm what applies to your teams. Jeeves also offers[global business accounts](https://www.tryjeeves.com/us-product/global-accounts) that hold USD, EUR, GBP and CAD, and the guide on[global expense management](https://www.tryjeeves.com/blog/global-expense-management) explains how to organize spending across entities and currencies.


## How do virtual cards connect to accounting?


Virtual cards connect to accounting when the provider syncs each transaction, with its category and receipt, to your accounting software. Jeeves connects directly to QuickBooks Online, Xero and NetSuite, assigning GL codes by merchant and category.


This matters at close. When every card has a name, a purpose and a coded category, the controller spends less time asking who paid for what and more time reviewing exceptions.


Receipts help too: the card owner can upload receipts from the mobile app or web, and Jeeves sends reminders for anything missing, as described on the[expense management](https://www.tryjeeves.com/us-product/expense-management) page. Ask your accountant which fields they need, such as vendor, category and project, and set up card names and categories to match before you issue many cards.


## What to look for in a virtual card provider: a checklist


To choose a virtual card provider, compare how cards are funded, the controls per card, how quickly cards can be issued, accounting integrations, country coverage, fees and eligibility, and support. The table lists what to ask.


What to check Questions to ask


Funding model Are cards pre-funded or funded another way? Where does the money come from?


Controls per card Can you set limits, merchant categories, vendors and dates for each card?


Speed of issuance How quickly can a new card be created and used?


Accounting integration Which tools does it connect to, and how are categories coded?


Country coverage Where can cards be issued, and in which currencies?


Fees and eligibility Are fees and eligibility rules available in writing?


Support Who helps when a card is declined or a limit needs to change?


Jeeves issues pre-funded virtual cards in several countries, with controls per card. Ask any provider to put fees and eligibility in writing. A good first step is to pilot a couple of cards, review how they work in practice and expand from there.


## Frequently asked questions about virtual cards for business


### What is a virtual card for business?


A virtual card for business is a digital card number issued for company spending, with no physical plastic. Finance teams assign it to an employee, vendor, project or subscription, set a limit and can freeze or cancel it at any time without affecting other cards.


### How do virtual corporate cards work?


A finance admin creates a card in a dashboard, names it, sets a limit and optional start and end dates, then shares the details or adds the card to a mobile wallet. Each payment is tied to that card, so spending can be tracked per employee, vendor or project.


### Is a virtual business credit card the same as a pre-funded virtual card?


No. A virtual credit card draws on a credit line that is repaid later, while a pre-funded virtual card spends only money already loaded into the account. Jeeves US cards are pre-funded and draw from your Jeeves Cash balance. There is no credit line behind them.


### How many virtual cards can a company issue with Jeeves?


Jeeves lets teams issue unlimited virtual cards. Many companies create one card per subscription, ad account, vendor or project so each becomes its own cost center and can be limited or closed independently.


### Are virtual cards safe for business spending?


Virtual cards are generally safer than sharing one card across a team because each card has its own number, limit and controls. If a card is exposed or no longer needed, finance can freeze or delete it without disrupting other payments.


### Can virtual cards be used for international or online platform spend?


Yes, virtual cards are commonly used for online and cross-border purchases such as software, advertising and cloud services. Jeeves issues local cards across the US, Canada, the UK, Europe, Mexico, Brazil and Colombia, managed from one dashboard.


### How do I choose a virtual card provider for my business?


Compare how the cards are funded, the controls available per card, how quickly cards can be issued, how transactions sync to accounting tools and where cards can be issued. Ask the provider to explain fees and eligibility in writing before you commit.


Virtual cards for business work best when each card has a clear purpose, a limit and a person responsible for it. Start with a few cards, review how they perform and expand from there. Jeeves is not a bank: it is a financial platform that provides payment and expense management services and technology solutions.
